docs.title: MSF TypeScript
docs.text: This package provides the shared TypeScript and JavaScript utility layer for MSF projects. It is built as a reusable library so teams can share conventions, common logic, and lightweight utilities without duplicating implementation across repositories.

docs.title: Package purpose
docs.text:
The library is intended to provide:

  • shared TypeScript/JavaScript utilities
  • package-level build and distribution conventions
  • reuse across multiple MSF repositories
  • a centralized place for common logic that should be versioned and published

docs.title: Repository shape
docs.text:
typescript/
├── src/
├── tests/
├── package.json
├── tsconfig.json
├── tsup.config.ts
├── vitest.config.ts
├── mkdocs.yml
├── .github/
└── openwiki/

docs.title: Typical commands
docs.text:
npm install
npm run build
npm run test
npm run lint

docs.title: Operational guidance
docs.text:
• keep utilities generic and broadly reusable
  • prefer small, stable API surfaces over large domain-specific helpers
  • document public exports clearly for downstream packages
  • validate the package before releasing any public changes

docs.title: Project overview
docs.text: The @msflib/typescript package provides the shared utility layer across the MSF ecosystem. It is oriented around portability, small public APIs, and consistent packaging so it can be reused across apps and libraries without forcing each repo to reinvent the same utility patterns.

docs.title: Main responsibilities
docs.text:
This package is designed to cover:

  • general TypeScript utilities
  • shared JavaScript runtime helpers
  • packaged release flow via build output in dist/
  • versioned reuse across the MSF libraries

docs.title: Package conventions
docs.text:
"main": "./dist/index.js",
"module": "./dist/index.mjs",
"types": "./dist/index.d.ts"

This helps downstream packages consume the library in both CommonJS and ESM contexts.

docs.title: Typical workflow
docs.text:
npm install
npm run build
npm run test
npm run lint

docs.title: Development guidance
docs.text:
• keep public APIs small and stable
  • document exported utilities clearly
  • prefer shared helpers over repo-local duplication
  • validate packaging and build output before release
